original_question: (J. Wiegold). Let Γ be a finite simple group and let Nn(Γ) denote the set of normal subgroups of the free group Fn of rank n whose quotient is isomorphic to Γ. Conjecture: Aut(Fn) acts transitively on Nn(Γ) for n ⩾ 3. This is not true for n = 2(B. H. Neumann, H. Neumann, Math. Nachr., 4(1951), 106–125).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.81 (J. Wiegold) in New Problems (21st issue, 2026): for a finite simple group Γ, let N_n(Γ) be the set of normal subgroups N of the free group F_n of rank n such that F_n/N is isomorphic to Γ; conjecturally, Aut(F_n) acts transitively on N_n(Γ) for n ≥ 3.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official formulation almost verbatim: it fixes a finite simple group Γ, defines N_n(Γ) as the set of normal subgroups of F_n with quotient isomorphic to Γ, states the conjectured transitivity of Aut(F_n) for n ≥ 3, and includes the paper's remark that the analogous statement is false for n = 2, with the cited Neumann-Neumann reference.
missing_details: Make the quantifiers completely explicit: the question is intended for every finite simple group Γ and every integer n ≥ 3.
To be fully stand-alone, specify the action of Aut(F_n) on N_n(Γ), namely α · N = α(N) for α in Aut(F_n).
Present N_n(Γ) in full set-builder form, N_n(Γ) = {N ◁ F_n : F_n/N ≅ Γ}, so the quotient condition is explicit without relying on prose.
Clarify that the sentence about n = 2 is background/counterexample context and not part of the conjecture's hypothesis range.
refined_question: For every finite simple group Γ and every integer n ≥ 3, let F_n be the free group of rank n and let N_n(Γ) = {N ◁ F_n : F_n/N ≅ Γ}. Is the natural action of Aut(F_n) on N_n(Γ), given by α · N = α(N), transitive? (The paper notes that the analogous statement is false for n = 2.)
justification: The draft is targeting exactly Problem 21.81, and not a broader neighboring statement. In the paper, 21.81 itself gives all the core notation and the conjecture in essentially the same words as your draft. There is no additional hidden hypothesis on Γ or on F_n stated there. The only sharpening needed is to make the universal quantifiers and the group action explicit so that the question is fully stand-alone. The adjacent Problem 21.82 is a different conjecture about finite simple characteristic quotients of F_n, so it should not be folded into the present question.
